statement: Find the stationary points of $y=x^{3}-3x^{2}-9x+5$ and determine their nature.
solution:
$$\frac{dy}{dx}=3x^{2}-6x-9=3(x^{2}-2x-3)=3(x-3)(x+1).$$
Stationary points at $x=3$ and $x=-1$.
The second derivative is $\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}=6x-6$.
At $x=3$: $\tfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}=12>0$, so a minimum; $y=27-27-27+5=-22$, giving $(3,-22)$.
At $x=-1$: $\tfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}=-12<0$, so a maximum; $y=-1-3+9+5=10$, giving $(-1,10)$.
hints: Differentiate and factorise the cubic derivative.
Set the derivative equal to zero.
Use the second derivative to classify each point.
